about: What each card Vitro draws natively supports: every option and value it draws exactly as Home Assistant does. A card whose config has anything else falls back (an island for a custom card, HA's frontend for a built-in one). Read by compat/NativeOptions.kt in the engine, site/src/lib/vitroCompat.ts and the audit script; the format is in NativeOptions.kt.

mushroomTemplate.why: a template reading user, config or area renders differently without Mushroom's variables
mushroomTemplate.note: Mushroom renders templates with the variables config and user (plus entity, and area on the template card), strict; Vitro's render_template gets only `entity` (a {% set %} prefix), so a template that reads user, config or area renders differently

mushroomTemplateIcon.why: as mushroomTemplate; an icon `weather-<condition>` (no mdi: prefix) draws Mushroom's weather SVG, Vitro an MDI glyph

mushroomRgbColor.why: Vitro reads Mushroom's color names and #hex only
mushroomRgbColor.note: Mushroom's computeRgbColor: a name from its COLORS or #hex; anything else (rgba(), CSS names) is invalid there and Mushroom keeps its default, where Vitro would draw it. light-grey/dark-grey aren't in Vitro's table; `disabled` is theme-dependent in Mushroom

mushroomCssColor.why: the template card (Mushroom 5) uses HA's computeCssColor: a theme color name or any CSS color

autoEntitiesValue.why: a match Vitro doesn't evaluate as auto-entities does
autoEntitiesValue.note: auto-entities 1.16.1 value match (Me): a numeric comparison, a /regex/, a * glob or an exact string. Left out: `!=` and `!` (parseFloat of '=5' is NaN, so the real card matches everything), comparisons with a non-number, a leading space before an operator (Vitro's COMPARE trims it, the real card doesn't), `$$` (JSON.stringify), 'N m/h/d ago', a value starting with / but not ending with it, and globs with regex characters (the real card doesn't escape them, Vitro does). Strings only: the real card compares a number or boolean with ===, Vitro coerces it

autoEntitiesState.why: auto-entities also matches the translated state; Vitro matches the raw state only
autoEntitiesState.note: the real `state` rule also matches the translated state (formatEntityState: 'On', 'Open', '21.5 °C'); Vitro matches only the raw state. So only numeric comparisons and lowercase raw-state tokens or globs; regexes and capitalized values could target the translation

reverse.why: without a method auto-entities sorts nothing, so reverse does nothing; Vitro reverses the list

count.why: count: 0 is falsy and ignored by auto-entities; Vitro shows nothing

reverse.why: the 'none' comparator returns 0, so the real card never reverses; Vitro does
entity ids never tie, so reversing the sorted list equals the reversed comparator

numeric.why: numeric: Vitro treats non-numbers as equal (no order); the real card compares them as strings

reverse.why: Vitro reverses the sorted list, which flips ties; the real card flips only the comparator (stable ties)
many entities share last_changed after an HA restart: ties

stackInCardKeep.why: Vitro draws only these combinations of stack-in-card's keep options as it does
stackInCardKeep.note: box_shadow: Vitro always takes the children's shadow off. border_radius without background: stack-in-card keeps the child's rounded border, but Vitro strokes it square (applySeamlessSurface)

cssBox.why: paddingDp reads em/rem as 16 px, unitless numbers as px, and drops negatives; only px and 0 behave as CSS does

grid-template-columns.why: tracks Vitro lays out as CSS grid does: fr, px or %, minmax() and repeat()
grid-template-columns.note: fr/px/% tracks, minmax(px|%|0, fr|px|%), repeat(<integer>, …). Left out: auto-fill/auto-fit (Vitro counts tracks against the display width, not the card's), auto and min-content (drawn as 1fr), em, calc, named lines, commas

grid-gap.why: one px value; Vitro uses the first number for both row and column gap

max_cols.why: 0 is falsy in layout-card (default 4, or 3 with a docked sidebar); Vitro clamps it to 1

min_height.why: 0 is falsy in layout-card (default 5); Vitro uses 0
